analysis.investment_thesis: B.R. Goyal Infra is a small-cap civil construction play riding India's infra capex cycle with 25.6% PAT CAGR and reasonable 8.4x P/E. However, negative FY25 OCF of -INR 36 Cr, modest 14% ROE, and EPC working-capital strain keep this as a "prove it" name rather than a high-conviction bet.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR 15% and PAT CAGR 26% (FY20-25) riding Gati Shakti/NHAI tailwind
Promoter holding strong at 73.6% with sound ROCE of 17.9%
Cheap optically at 8.4x P/E and ~1.1x P/B post-equity raise
key_risks: FY25 OCF -INR 36 Cr and FCF -INR 58 Cr — working capital bleed despite reported profits
Revenue fell 13% in FY25 (589→510 Cr) — lumpy EPC order book
Small regional EPC player with no moat; dependent on government payment cycles
red_flags: Financing CF +INR 92 Cr in FY25 funding negative operating cash — equity-raise-fueled growth
Borrowings jumped 57% (49→77 Cr) in FY25 even after capital raise
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is a classic small-cap EPC story riding India's road and infrastructure capex wave — the sector tailwind is real with NHAI awards, Gati Shakti, and state highway programs. Topline moved from INR 225 Cr (FY22) to INR 589 Cr (FY24) and net profit compounded at 26%, which is respectable. At 8.4x P/E and ~1.1x P/B (270 Cr mcap vs 245 Cr equity), valuation isn't demanding. Promoter holding at 73.6% is comforting — they have skin in the game.\n\nBut I've seen this movie in infra: receivables balloon, OCF turns negative, and small EPC players get squeezed by government payment cycles. FY25's -INR 36 Cr operating cash flow against INR 25 Cr reported profit is a red flag — profits on paper, cash elsewhere. Revenue also declined 13% in FY25. For a concentrated bet I need dominant scale (L&T, KNR) or a differentiated niche — B.R. Goyal is neither. HOLD; wait for two consecutive quarters of positive OCF before adding conviction.
